# Chris Orlob Voice Corpus

Research date: 2026-09-09

The excerpts below are short quotations from public Gong.io and pclub.io blog posts and YouTube training videos, included under fair use for style analysis and attribution. They are third-party content and NOT covered by this repository's MIT license.

**Provenance note.** Items 1-27 were read directly from gong.io (via the Wayback Machine) and pclub.io/Caliber on the research date and are verbatim. Items 28-35 come from YouTube auto-generated (ASR) caption tracks of Chris Orlob training videos and are labeled `documented`; wording may contain transcription artifacts (for example "rammed" for "ramped"), so treat exact phrasing as approximate even though the content and numbers are his.

**Punctuation note.** Item 12 preserves an em dash because it is a verbatim quotation from the original post. The operator's copy rule still bans em and en dashes in anything generated in this voice; see the Punctuation Override in SKILL.md.

## Verbatim excerpts

### From "The 11 Best Discovery Call Tips for Sales You'll Read This Year" (gong.io/blog, March 28, 2019, via Wayback Machine)

1. "Discovery is a process, not an event"
   Section header, Discovery Call Tip #1. https://web.archive.org/web/20190915055818/https://www.gong.io/blog/best-discovery-call-tips/

2. "The best discovery calls I hear don't sound like discovery."
   Callout he features approvingly in the post, printed as a standalone line worth "printing out."

3. "Can you help me understand your biggest challenge?"
   His fix for the flat version, "What's your biggest challenge?" - the reframe that signals he wants a long answer.

4. "Buyer: We're losing deals to competitors. Our product is strong, but our reps back peddle when customers ask how we're different. You: Back peddle?"
   Worked example of mirroring, rendered as a Buyer:/You: transcript.

5. "It sounds like you feel overwhelmed every time a new onboarding class starts."
   Worked example of labeling, a Chris Voss technique he credits by name.

6. "Can you walk me through your sales process, from when you first generate a new lead, through to a closed deal?"
   His own discovery question from his rep days, contrasted with the "trite" version, "What's your sales process?"

7. "There's a sweet spot for how many discovery questions you should ask during a sales call. That number is between 11 and 14."
   The data-slap number that anchors Tip #9.

8. "successful meetings with C-suite executives have only four questions on average. Unsuccessful meetings have eight."
   Call-analysis stat on executive discovery fatigue.

## Documented (ASR caption tracks, from YouTube training videos)

Wording may contain minor transcription errors; numbers and content are his, exact phrasing is approximate.

28. "What metric is suffering as a result of that."
    The word-for-word question he teaches for quantifying pain, from a "cost of inaction" training video. `documented`

29. "Ten times forty thousand dollars, fully ramped reps, that's 400 grand knocked off of your annual plan a year from now."
    His worked example: a $50,000 SaaS deal negotiation where he built a cost-of-inaction case instead of discounting. `documented`

30. "Helped grow a company called Gong from two hundred thousand dollars to over 200 million dollars in total annual revenue and a 7.2 billion dollar valuation... in the span of about five and a half years."
    His standard credential drop before teaching content. `documented`

31. "Write that down. Money follows pain."
    His recurring maxim, repeated across at least two videos in this corpus. `documented`

32. "Can you help me understand the challenges you're facing that would derail you if you didn't solve them?"
    His outbound-discovery kickstart question. `documented`

33. "What challenge is going on in your business that's driving this to be a priority?"
    The "peel back the onion" follow-up he uses to move from surface answer to strategic urgency. `documented`

34. "There's a behavioral scientist named Daniel Kahneman. He's done a bunch of research on this, where the pain of loss is twice as intense emotionally than the pleasure from gain."
    Cited research backing his "money follows pain" maxim. `documented`

35. "Selling is an act of leadership."
    From a video on the nine bad habits keeping SaaS sellers off the leaderboard. `documented`

## Structural notes for the writer

- Post and video titles state an exact count: "The 11 Best...", "7 Elements of...", "9 Habits That...". The count is never rounded.
- Almost every claim carries a number pulled from call or demo analysis, never a vague "most reps" without a percentage attached somewhere nearby.
- Dialogue is a real formatting device, same as April Dunford's, but here it demonstrates a call mechanic (mirroring, labeling) rather than a customer-discovery story.
- He credits Chris Voss by name for mirroring and labeling, and Daniel Kahneman by name for loss aversion. Named sourcing is part of the voice.
- His own Gong growth story ($200K to $200M ARR, 5.5 years) and his own deal negotiations are his proof, repeated close to verbatim across multiple pieces of content.
- pclub.io posts sell the course/community inside the content itself ("Get our premiere online course...", "Join the Platinum Passport..."). Older gong.io posts sell the free training video instead.
